title: Randomizer
statementMd:
Gerald got tired of playing board games with the usual six-sided die, and he bought a toy called Randomizer. It functions as follows.

A Randomizer has its own coordinate plane on which a strictly convex polygon is painted, the polygon is called a **basic polygon**. If you shake a Randomizer, it draws some nondegenerate (i.e. having a non-zero area) convex polygon with vertices at some vertices of the **basic polygon**. The result of the roll (more precisely, the result of the shaking) is considered to be the number of points with integer coordinates, which were strictly inside (the points on the border are not considered) the selected polygon. Now Gerald is wondering: what is the expected result of shaking the Randomizer?

During the shaking the Randomizer considers all the possible non-degenerate convex polygons with vertices at the vertices of the **basic polygon**. Let's assume that there are $*k*$ versions of the polygons. Then the Randomizer chooses each of them with probability ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/22feb005334cd9870463a00bec8551fb6ba542cc.png).

## Input

The first line of the input contains a single integer $*n*$ ($3 ≤ *n* ≤ 100 000$) — the number of vertices of the basic polygon.

Next $*n*$ lines contain the coordinates of the vertices of the basic polygon. The $*i*$-th of these lines contain two integers $*x*_{*i*}$ and $*y*_{*i*}$ ($- 10^{9} ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *y*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — the coordinates of the $*i*$-th vertex of the polygon. The vertices are given in the counter-clockwise order.

## Output

Print the sought expected value with absolute or relative error at most $10^{ - 9}$.

## Note

A polygon is called strictly convex if it is convex and no its vertices lie on the same line.

Let's assume that a random variable takes values $*x*_{1}, ..., *x*_{*n*}$ with probabilities $*p*_{1}, ..., *p*_{*n*}$, correspondingly. Then the expected value of this variable equals to ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e592ba0986f3722e82626df9d579add61ddc5d36.png).
statementZhMd:
Gerald 厌倦了使用普通的六面骰子玩桌游，于是他买了一个名为 Randomizer 的玩具。它的工作方式如下。

Randomizer 有自己的坐标平面，平面上绘制着一个严格凸多边形，该多边形称为**基本多边形**。当你摇动 Randomizer 时，它会从**基本多边形**的某些顶点中选取顶点，构成一个非退化（即面积非零）的凸多边形。摇动的结果（更准确地说，是摇动后得到的结果）定义为严格位于所选多边形内部的整点数量（边界上的点不计入）。现在 Gerald 想知道：摇动 Randomizer 的期望结果是多少？

在摇动过程中，Randomizer 会考虑所有顶点为**基本多边形**顶点的非退化凸多边形。假设这样的多边形共有 $*k*$ 个。那么 Randomizer 会以概率 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/22feb005334cd9870463a00bec8551fb6ba542cc.png) 等概率地选择其中一个。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$3 ≤ *n* ≤ 100 000$），表示基本多边形的顶点数。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行包含基本多边形的顶点坐标。第 $*i*$ 行包含两个整数 $*x*_{*i*}$ 和 $*y*_{*i*}$（$- 10^{9} ≤ *x*_{*i*}, *y*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$），表示多边形第 $*i*$ 个顶点的坐标。顶点按照逆时针顺序给出。

## 输出格式

输出所求的期望值。若答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 $10^{ - 9}$，则视为正确。

## 说明

如果一个多边形是凸多边形，且不存在三个顶点共线，则称其为严格凸多边形。

假设一个随机变量分别以概率 $*p*_{*1*}$、$...$、$*p*_{*n*}$ 取值 $*x*_{*1*}$、$...$、$*x*_{*n*}$。那么该随机变量的期望值等于 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e592ba0986f3722e82626df9d579add61ddc5d36.png)。
